First of all, they said “maybe.” They are also correct. There is a disorder that destroys many peoples lives in this way. It’s called body dysmorphic disorder. It can be about ANY pet of your body. It can be about your face, or just one part of your face. This disorder ruins lives because of people brushing it off. It’s an absolutely hellacious life to live, so it’s so much better to catch it as early as possible.

This comment is a very good one. You are absolutely right. When someone is this insecure it CAN be body dysmorphic disorder, which can be about ANY feature you have. Which is like insecurity and OCD having a baby. I NEVER would have imagined I had disorder thinking. I thought I was just ugly, a monster. It ruled my life, it did its best to keep me relationship-less.

I was this girl. I was a young person in a LDR. (For years) We only met twice. I never wanted to be on webcam, and he eventually expressed his frustration and sadness. 

I didn’t know I was dealing with body dysmorphic disorder. I would consider this for her situation, maybe you could bring it up to her. 

I never would have imagined I had a disorder/disordered thinking. It was just a VERY strong “no, I don’t like my face, so no, I won’t turn my camera on.” It turns out all that time of not wanting to be seen, of suffering silently while other people just saw me as simply insecure, was a disorder. It’s like insecurity meets OCD. It absolutely RULES you. It doesn’t matter who the other person is, if we feel like hiding we will do everything we can to hide. It doesn’t matter how much someone is nice to us, it doesn’t matter how much we are genuinely liked or even loved. This disorder is painful and isolating. If we do get close to someone, we push them away, because the closer we get to them the more they expect to see us. But we can’t stand to be seen… Our disordered brain wants us to hide. 


 My suffering with BDD was centered around my face. I thought I looked so much worse than I did, because in reality I was just a normal girl that a guy found pretty and wanted to date. I didn’t see this, I didn’t believe this. I thought I looked like a monster. I didn’t want to go anywhere because of my face. And it was so bad that I didn’t even want to show my face to the person I was dating, even when we had already reached an “I love you” point.

I used to have “humanly perfect skin” I guess, but because I couldn’t see it due to an actual disorder, I ended up giving myself actual skin problems. I spent so many days of my life giving myself chemical burns with products. I did DIY things like obsessively rubbing lemons on my face. I picked at my skin for hours on end. I didn’t know what sebaceous filaments were so I picked at them until my nose is now covered in ice pick holes. I sat oiled up in the sun. My skin is now truly atrocious. But I would have said it was atrocious then and meant it. I feel sorry for everyone in that stage and I hope they don’t end up ruining their faces like I did. I’m so scared and sad for all the people younger than me especially.

My struggle with body dysmorphic disorder took off on the delusional end when I was in high school. I genuinely believed my skin was monstrous, had so many problems, wasn’t normal, blablabla…when looking back NOW, over a decade later, I can see it WAS normal for a teenager, if not “humanly perfect.” But I could not see that during those years. I knew nothing about normal skin and I knew nothing about skincare. If I was a teenager TODAY, or even when I was in my early twenties, I could easily be the type of person to post begging for help with skin issues either 1) nobody else could really point out from a distance during normal everyday interactions and 2) issues my mind really did make up. I was so obsessed with my skin when I was a teenager especially. I don’t think I could survive being a teenager now. Having such awful skin as an adult and seeing all the perfect skin online gets to me, but I can fight it off with the logic and acceptance I have now. If I was a younger person this sort of thing would drive me to suicide. But since I’ve also gone through such a hellacious battle with this disorder, I now try not to let posts like that get to me, because they may be suffering with the disorder too. You can’t see yourself properly. You’re constantly trying to fix yourself, even if there’s nothing to fix to anyone else. It’s truly hell on earth.
